  • LTX-2.3

  • ComfyUI / Colab / Kaggle GPU servers

It should support up to five independently configured API servers, rather than relying on one fixed URL.

How I’ll make the server handling work

  1. Add a server-management section where you can register up to five API URLs, each with its own API key and workflow ID.

  2. Store each server’s URL, key, workflow ID and status in the database—not duplicate them in .env or config.py.

  3. When generating a video, iterate through the registered servers and select an available FREE worker.

  4. Mark that worker BUSY before submitting the API request.

  5. Monitor the job and retrieve its output.

  6. Mark the worker FREE after completion or failure, so it can handle another job.

  7. Show each server's connection status, current workload and errors in the UI.

The important point: the system should not send the same generation job to all five GPUs simultaneously. It should distribute jobs across available workers, avoiding a busy server.

One important detail before I implement the worker manager:

I recommend storing separate workflow IDs for LTX-2.3 and LTX-2.5 Pose for each server. That way, the system can select a FREE server that actually supports the requested video model.
